body.p: Claims 1-20 are pending. Applicant has amended claims 1, 3, 15, and 20 and canceled claim 2 and 16. The amendments are made without disclaimer of subject matter, and the Applicant reserves the right to pursue subject matter of any previously pending claim in a continuation or divisional application. No new matter has been introduced. Support for the amendments can be found throughout the specification, for example, at paragraphs [0081]- [0083] and original claim 2. The Applicant requests reconsideration in light of the amendment to the claims and the following remarks. II. Objection to Drawings

The Examiner objected to the drawings because they do not include reference signs mentioned in the description. Applicant has amended the drawings to address the objections. III. Rejection under 35 U.S.C. §§ 102 and 103

Amended independent claim 1 recites determining desired center-of-mass motion data of the robot based on the center-of-mass reference trajectory, the desired center-of-mass motion data being a desired value of motion data associated with a center of mass of the robot; constructing an objective function based on the desired center-of-mass motion data and matrix data constructed based on a position relationship between the center of mass of the robot and contact points, the contact points being contact points between the robot and an environment, a value of the objective function is representing a degree of deviation of the robot from the center-of-mass reference trajectoiy; and calculating center-of-mass control information enabling the value of the objective function to satisfy an optimization stop condition.

As conceded by the Examiner, Ha fails to teach to calculate center-of-mass control information enabling the value of the objective function constructed based on the desired center-of-mass motion data to satisfy an optimization stop condition. In reliance upon paragraph [0076] of Rinke, the Examiner asserted that Rinke teaches the above limitations.

Amended claim 1 further requires that the objective function is constructed based on the desired center-of-mass motion data and matrix data constructed based on a position relationship between the center of mass of the robot and contact points between the robot and an environment. Rinke simply teaches a differential-alebraic equations (DAE) to retarget motion profiles of the physical robot to minimize the dynamic equilibrium constant to minimize deviations. [0076] of Rinke. However, Rinke fails to disclose or teach that the DAE takes into account the matrix data constructed based on a position relationship between the center of mass of the robot and contact points between the robot and an environment. Indeed, Rinke does not mention contact points. Therefore, Ha and Rinke fail to disclose, teach, or suggest calculating center-of-mass control information enabling the value of the objective function, constructed based on the desired center-of-mass motion data and matrix data constructed based on a position relationship between the center of mass of the robot and contact points, to satisfy an optimization stop condition, as claimed in amended claim 1.

For at least these reasons, amended independent claim 1, and any claim that depends from claim 1, is patentable over Ha as contemplated by the Examiner, alone or in the proposed combination with Rinke. Independent claims 11 and 20 are amended to recite similar features as the amended claim 1. For similar reasons as the amended claim 1, amended independent claims 15 and 20, any claim that depends from claims 15, are patentable over Ha as contemplated by the Examiner, alone or in the proposed combination with Rinke.

In view of the amendments to the claims and the foregoing remarks, Applicant submits that the pending claims are in condition for allowance. Reconsideration is therefore respectfully requested. The Examiner is invited to contact the undersigned attorney for the Applicant via telephone if such communication would expedite this application.
